transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Please tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I came in because I just can't seem to shut my brain off anymore. It's like... it always starts with just one small concern. Say a client isn't responding to an email. But within minutes, my mind just races and I'm convinced I'm going to lose the contract. And then I start thinking I'll fall behind on my divorce payments, and from there I'm suddenly sure I'll never get back to a real leadership role at work. It just spirals like that, and I can't stop it.
Do you find that your worrying happens most days and is difficult to control, or does it come and go depending on the situation?

It's most days. It doesn't really come and go, it's just... there. And yeah, it is very difficult to control. My mind just keeps jumping from contract work to my mortgage payments, or... or worrying about whether people in the Bethesda tech circles think I'm damaged goods. I can't seem to reel it in. Even just a delayed email from a recruiter can feel like proof that my whole career is closing down.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like restlessness, trouble sleeping, muscle tension, or irritability along with these worries?

Yeah, definitely the restlessness and the muscle tension. I just feel wound up almost all day. It's like my shoulders are completely locked... like I'm just braced and ready for bad news. And I can't really sit still. I end up pacing around the house a lot, or if I'm on a work call, I'm constantly bouncing my leg, even when nothing is actually happening. It's just this constant physical edge.
Have you found yourself losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or feeling down or hopeless a lot of the time?

No, I wouldn't say I feel hopeless or down like that. I still want to do the things I usually enjoy, I just... I'm usually too keyed up to actually relax and do them. But the interest is still there. I'm just more anxious than sad, I guess.
Have you been feeling fatigued or low on energy lately, even if you haven’t been physically active?

No, not really. I mean, I'm tired sometimes because I don't sleep great with all the worrying, but I wouldn't say I feel fatigued or completely drained of energy during the day. It's more that I'm just constantly tense rather than exhausted.
Do you find yourself worrying about a number of different things, rather than just one specific issue, even when there isn't an immediate problem?

Yeah, it's definitely not just one thing. My mind just keeps jumping around all over the place. I'll be worrying about my contract work, and then... then I'm stressing out about the mortgage payments. And then I start overthinking whether people in the Bethesda tech circles think I'm damaged goods or something. 

It doesn't even take a real crisis to set it off. Like, if a recruiter is just a little delayed in replying to an email, it suddenly feels like absolute proof that my whole career is closing down. It's just a constant cycle of different worries.
Do you find that your anxiety and worry are present even when there isn't a specific or immediate problem to address?

Yeah, like I was just saying, it really doesn't take an actual crisis. Even if it's a quiet day and there's no immediate problem staring me in the face, the worry is still... just there. It's like my mind is always waiting for the other shoe to drop, even when everything is technically fine at that exact moment.
